1	\chapter{The identity component of the Picard scheme}
     2	\label{chap:Picard_IdentityComponent}
     3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/IdentityComponent.lean
     4	\providecommand{\connComp}{\operatorname{Comp}}
     5	
     6	% STRATEGY NOTE (iter-184). This chapter is the A.3 sub-row of Route~A
     7	% (positive-genus arm of \texttt{nonempty\_jacobianWitness}). It builds the
     8	% identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) of the Picard scheme as an
     9	% open-and-closed subgroup scheme of \(\Pic_{C/k}\), equips it with the
    10	% degree-zero characterisation, and identifies it as an abelian variety
    11	% of dimension \(g(C)\). The abstract identity-component substrate
    12	% (\cref{def:identity_component_group_scheme} +
    13	% \cref{thm:identity_component_open_subgroup}) is new project material:
    14	% the Lean target
    15	% \texttt{AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent} does not yet
    16	% exist in Mathlib.
    17	%
    18	% NOTE: future split candidate when a second consumer materialises. The
    19	% abstract identity-component substrate is kept in this chapter (rather
    20	% than split off into a separate
    21	% \texttt{GroupScheme\_IdentityComponent.tex}) because it is small and
    22	% has a single consumer for now. If a second consumer materialises,
    23	% revisit the split.
    24	
    25	% STATUS (run 0009). The Lean target file
    26	% \texttt{AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/IdentityComponent.lean} exists; the
    27	% \S 1 group-scheme substrate (identity-component definition and its four
    28	% conclusion-specific theorems) is fully proved. Remaining sorries are
    29	% confined to \S 3--\S 4. The mathematical degree rows have no exact Lean
    30	% pins; \texttt{finrank\_eq\_genus} and \texttt{kPoints\_iff\_kerDegree}
    31	% remain typed sorries downstream of the FGA representability foundation
    32	% (\texttt{AJC.picrep}).
    33	
    34	\section{Setup and motivation}
    35	\label{sec:pic0_setup}
    36	
    37	Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper
    38	geometrically integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) of genus \(g = g(C)\)
    39	(\cref{def:genus}). Write \(\Pic^{\et}_{C/k}\) for a \(k\)-scheme
    40	representing the \'etale-sheafified relative Picard functor
    41	\(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) of \cref{def:pic_et_sheaf}. Its existence over an
    42	arbitrary field, with no rational-point hypothesis, is the open theorem
    43	\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability_etale}. It is separated and locally of
    44	finite type over \(k\), and its degree pieces form a disjoint union of open
    45	quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes.
    46	
    47	The Lean-pinned \(\Pic_{C/k}\) and \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) below instead use the
    48	legacy scheme representing the unsheafified \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\), conditional
    49	on its separate representability hypotheses. They are not identified here
    50	with \(\Pic^{\et}_{C/k}\); the arbitrary-field degree statements use the
    51	superscript \(\et\) explicitly.
    52	
    53	The identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) singled out by Kleiman is the open
    54	and closed subgroup scheme consisting of the connected component of
    55	\(\Pic_{C/k}\) containing the trivial line bundle. It is the locus of
    56	degree-zero classes, and on a smooth proper curve it is itself an
    57	abelian variety of dimension \(g\) --- the Jacobian variety of \(C\). This
    58	chapter packages those four statements as the A.3 specification.
    59	
    60	\section{The identity component of a group scheme}
   815	  \leanok
   816	  \uses{lem:geometricallyConnected_of_connected_of_section, def:identity_component_section, lem:identity_component_section_is_section, lem:identity_component_connected}

   827	\section{The identity component of the Picard scheme}
   828	\label{sec:pic0_definition}
   829	
   830	We now specialise the abstract identity-component construction to the
   831	conditional legacy representer \(G = \Pic_{C/k}\) of
   832	\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\). This Lean-pinned specialization is distinct from the
   833	arbitrary-field \(\Pic^{\et}_{C/k}\) used in the degree rows below.
   834	
   835	\begin{definition}[The identity component of the Picard scheme]\leanok
   836	  \label{def:pic_zero_subscheme}
   837	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme}
   838	  \uses{def:identity_component_group_scheme, def:pic_scheme,
   839	    def:pic_scheme_lft, thm:pic_is_group_scheme}
   840	  % NOTE (run-0008): the Lean body is now REAL —
   841	  % Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C) — because
   842	  % the two gate instances landed with the run-0008 FGA rewire: the group
   843	  % structure GrpObj (PicScheme C) is genuinely proved (Yoneda transport,
   844	  % thm:pic_is_group_scheme) and local finiteness is the typed-sorry
   845	  % carrier def:pic_scheme_lft. The former raw-sorry body is gone; all §1
   846	  % substrate theorems now apply to Pic^0_{C/k} definitionally. The Lean
   847	  % signature carries [HasPicScheme C] [PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C].
   848	
   849	  % SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 5, opening + Prp.~5.3;
   850	  % arXiv:math/0504020, p.~36 (read from
   851	  % references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex, L2836-L2841 +
   852	  % L2921-L2929).
   853	  % SOURCE QUOTE:
   854	  % "Having treated the existence of the Picard scheme \(\IPic_{X/S}\), we now
   855	  % turn to its structure.  In this section, we study the union
   856	  % \(\IPicz_{X/S}\) of the connected components of the identity element,
   857	  % \(\IPicz_{X_s/k_s}\), for \(s\in S\)."
   858	  % SOURCE QUOTE:
   859	  % "\begin{prp}\label{prp:pic0}
   860	  %   Assume \(S\) is the spectrum of a field \(k\).  Assume \(\IPic_{X/k}\)
   861	  % exists and represents \(\Pic_{(X/k)\fppf}\).  Then \(\IPic_{X/k}\) is
   862	  % separated, and it is smooth if it has a geometrically reduced open
   863	  % subscheme.  Furthermore, the connected component of the identity
   864	  % \(\IPicz_{X/k}\) is an open and closed group subscheme of finite type; it
   865	  % is geometrically irreducible; and forming it commutes with extending
   866	  % \(k\).
   867	  %  \end{prp}"
   868	  \textit{Source: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 5, opening +
   869	  Prp.~5.3.}
   870	  Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field
   871	  \(k\), and assume the legacy relative Picard functor
   872	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) is represented by \(\Pic_{C/k}\). The
   873	  \emph{identity component of the Picard scheme}
   874	  \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is the identity component
   875	  \((\Pic_{C/k})^0\) of the \(k\)-group scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\) of
   876	  \cref{def:pic_scheme}, in the sense of
   877	  \cref{def:identity_component_group_scheme}. By
   878	  \cref{thm:identity_component_open_subgroup}, \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is an open
   879	  and closed subgroup scheme of \(\Pic_{C/k}\) of finite type over \(k\),
   880	  geometrically irreducible, and its formation commutes with
   881	  extension of the base field.
   882	\end{definition}
   883	
   884	\section{The degree map}
   885	\label{sec:pic_degree}
   886	
   887	Return now to the arbitrary-field representer \(\Pic^{\et}_{C/k}\) of
   888	\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability_etale}. Its disjoint open pieces are indexed
   889	by the Hilbert polynomial \(\Phi\) used in the FGA construction. With
   890	\(\mathcal H\) the chosen very ample invertible sheaf and \(\mathcal L\) the
   891	Picard representative, that construction uses the dual convention
   892	\[
   893	  \Phi_{\mathcal L}(n)
   894	  =\chi(C,\mathcal L^{-1}\otimes\mathcal H^{\otimes n})
   895	  =-\deg\mathcal L+n\deg\mathcal H+1-g.
   896	\]
   897	Thus its leading coefficient is \(\deg\mathcal H\), while
   898	\(\deg\mathcal L=-(\Phi_{\mathcal L}(0)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C))\). Intrinsically,
   899	\(\deg\mathcal L=\chi(C,\mathcal L)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)\), equivalently the
   900	coefficient of \(n\) in \(n\mapsto\chi(C,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})\). This
   901	identifies the geometric connected components of
   902	\(\Pic^{\et}_{C/k}\times_k\overline k\) with the integers, the index being the
   903	degree, without choosing a degree-one polarisation.
   904	
   905	\begin{definition}[Degree of a Picard class]\notready
   906	  \label{def:divisor_degree_pic}
   907	  \uses{def:pic_et_sheaf, def:hilbert_polynomial,
   908	    thm:fga_pic_representability_etale}
   909	
   910	  % SOURCE: [Milne], ``Abelian Varieties'' (course notes, 2008),
   911	  % \S III.1, ``Definitions and main statements'', p.~88 (PDF p.~94)
   912	  % (read from references/abelian-varieties.pdf).
   913	  % SOURCE QUOTE:

    12	/-!
    13	# The identity component of the Picard scheme
    14	
    15	Let `G` be a `k`-group scheme locally of finite type. Its **identity
    16	component** `G⁰` is the connected component of `|G|` containing the image of
    17	the identity section. It is an open and closed subgroup scheme of `G`, of
    18	finite type and geometrically irreducible over `k`, and its formation
    19	commutes with extension of the base field (Kleiman, §5, Lem.~`lem:agps`).
    20	
    21	This file develops that substrate for an arbitrary `k`-group scheme (§1) and
    22	then specialises it to the conditional legacy `PicSharp` representer
    23	`PicScheme C` (§2). Section §3 contains only candidate integer maps at the
    24	trivial legacy test object; it does not construct the arbitrary-test degree on
    25	the étale-sheafified Picard functor. The corresponding degree-zero
    26	characterisation in §4 remains open and is not faithfully typed by its legacy
    27	approximation.
    28	
    29	## Main results
    30	
    31	- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` — the identity component
    32	  `G⁰` of a `k`-group scheme `G` locally of finite type, as a `k`-scheme (an
    33	  object of `Over (Spec k)`): the open subscheme of `G` carried by the
    34	  connected component of the image of the identity section.
    35	- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme` —
    36	  the inclusion `G⁰ ↪ G` is both an open and a closed immersion.
    37	- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism` —
    38	  `G⁰` inherits the group-object structure of `G`.
    39	- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.baseChangeIso` — for a
    40	  field extension `K/k`, the base change `(G⁰)_K` is isomorphic to `(G_K)⁰`.
    41	- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`
    42	  — `G⁰` is of finite type and geometrically irreducible over `k`.
    43	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme` — the identity component
    44	  `Pic⁰_{C/k}` of the Picard scheme.
    45	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.degree` — a conditional totalisation of
    46	  an additive candidate at the legacy trivial test object, available only from
    47	  `[ClassDegreePinned C]` and set arbitrarily to `0` off sections.
    48	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme.finrank_eq_genus` — the dimension of
    49	  `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is the genus of `C`.
    50	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme.kPoints_iff_kerDegree` — the current
    51	  conditional, typed-sorry approximation to the degree-zero characterisation;
    52	  it is not an exact encoding of the classical statement on `k`-points.
    53	
    54	The abelian-variety identification of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (smooth, proper,
    55	geometrically irreducible `k`-group scheme of dimension `g(C)`) is assembled
    56	in the sibling file `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`.
    57	
    58	## Remaining obligations
    59	
    60	The §1 substrate for an abstract `k`-group scheme is unconditional. The open
    61	residues downstream of arbitrary-field étale Picard representability are
    62	mathematically distinct:
    63	
    64	- a genuine signed family degree: an additive natural transformation whose
    65	  fibre value is `χ(C_t, L_t) - χ(C_t, O_{C_t})`, locally constant on arbitrary
    66	  test schemes and invariant under the relative Picard quotient. The existing
    67	  `ClassDegreePinned` interface does not provide these properties.
    68	- `Pic0Scheme.finrank_eq_genus`: the equality
    69	  `dim Pic⁰_{C/k} = dim_k H¹(C, O_C) = g(C)`, which follows from
    70	  Picard smoothness plus the tangent-space/dimension comparison. It does not
    71	  depend on extracting a representing line bundle from a `k`-point.
    72	- `Pic0Scheme.kPoints_iff_kerDegree`: the identification of the `k`-points of
    73	  the legacy `Pic⁰_{C/k}` approximation with candidate-value-zero classes;
    74	  its current type is not the arbitrary-field mathematical statement.

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",
